title: NIS2 Directive + UK NIS Regulations 2025 Cross-Reference

eu.name: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 — NIS2
eu.full_title: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 December 2022 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2 Directive)

uk.name: The Network and Information Systems (Amendment and Transitional Provision) Regulations 2025
uk.authority: UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT)

overview.eu_nis2: NIS2 is the EU-wide cybersecurity legislation that replaces the original NIS Directive (2016/1148). It expands the scope of sectors, introduces stricter incident reporting timelines, enforces supply chain security, and imposes accountability on senior management. The directive harmonises cybersecurity requirements across member states with minimum harmonisation, allowing member states to adopt stricter measures.
overview.uk_nis_2025: The UK NIS Regulations 2025 are the post-Brexit evolution of the UK's implementation of the original NIS Directive (SI 2018/506). They maintain alignment with NIS2 in several areas while diverging on scope and enforcement. The 2025 regulations tighten incident reporting (from 72h to 24h for significant incidents), expand sector definitions, and increase maximum penalties to align with the EU regime for essential entities operating cross-border.

applicable_to: All medium and large enterprises in covered sectors
Public administration entities at central and regional level
DNS service providers, TLD registries, cloud computing providers
Data centre service providers, content delivery networks
Trust service providers, electronic communications networks
eu_nis2.size_threshold: Medium enterprises (50+ employees and/or €10M+ annual turnover) unless in critical sectors with no size exemption

critical: Energy (electricity, oil, gas, district heating/cooling, hydrogen)
Digital infrastructure (IXPs, DNS, TLDs, cloud, CDN, data centres)
ICT service management (managed service providers, managed security providers)
important: Manufacturing, production and distribution of chemicals
Production, processing and distribution of food
Manufacturing (medical devices, electronic/optical equipment, machinery, motor vehicles, transport equipment)
Digital providers (online marketplaces, search engines, social networks)

eu_nis2.territorial_scope: Any entity established in the EU, regardless of whether the service is provided within the EU

applicable_to: Essential services operators in energy, transport, health, drinking water, digital infrastructure
Relevant digital service providers (RDSPs) including cloud, online marketplaces, search engines
Managed service providers (MSPs) — expanded scope in 2025 regulations
Public sector bodies (central government departments, devolved administrations)
uk_nis_2025.territorial_scope: UK-established entities providing services within the UK

eu_nis2: Cybersecurity risk management measures (Article 21): entities must implement technical, operational and organisational measures to manage cybersecurity risks, including policies on risk analysis, incident handling, business continuity, supply chain security, network security, access control, encryption, and human resources security

Incident reporting (Article 23): submit (a) early warning within 24 hours, (b) incident notification within 72 hours, (c) intermediate report on request, (d) final report within one month of the incident resolution
Supply chain security (Article 21(2)(d)): include cybersecurity requirements in supply chain relationships, assess the security of suppliers and service providers
Use of certified ICT products (Article 24): member states shall promote the use of European cybersecurity certification schemes under the Cybersecurity Act
Senior management accountability (Article 20): management bodies must approve and oversee cybersecurity measures, receive training, and can be held personally liable for non-compliance

Security for network and information systems (Article 18): member states shall ensure essential and important entities take appropriate and proportionate technical, operational and organisational measures
Registration and database (Article 3(3)): member states maintain a national registry of essential and important entities
Peer review mechanism (Article 31): member states participate in a voluntary peer review process to assess CSIRT capabilities
uk_nis_2025: Risk management measures equivalent to NIS2 Article 21: technical and organisational measures appropriate to the risk
Incident reporting: early warning of significant incidents within 24 hours (reduced from 72h in NIS 2018), full report within 72 hours
Supply chain risk management: assess and manage cybersecurity risks from suppliers and third-party service providers
Senior management oversight: directors and equivalent must approve cybersecurity measures and can face personal liability for persistent non-compliance
Registration with the relevant Competent Authority (CESG/NCSC for digital infrastructure, sector regulators for others)
Annual compliance assessment: regulated entities must undergo periodic compliance audits
Business continuity and disaster recovery: documented plans tested at least annually

eu_nis2.essential_entities: Up to €10,000,000 or 2% of total annual worldwide turnover, whichever is higher (Article 34)
eu_nis2.important_entities: Up to €7,000,000 or 1.4% of total annual worldwide turnover, whichever is higher (Article 34)
eu_nis2.personal_liability: Senior management can face individual administrative fines and disqualification orders in serious cases
supervisory_measures: Temporary suspension of operations or authorisations

uk_nis_2025.essential_services: Up to £17,000,000 or 4% of qualifying turnover, whichever is higher
uk_nis_2025.rdsp_penalties: Up to £17,000,000 or 4% of worldwide turnover for non-compliance
uk_nis_2025.individual_liability: Directors can face disqualification for persistent or serious breaches
supervisory_measures: Enforcement notices requiring specific remedial actions
Prosecution for criminal offences in cases of deliberate non-compliance

eu_nis2.stage_1_early_warning: Within 24 hours of becoming aware — initial notification
eu_nis2.stage_4_final: Within 1 month of incident resolution — final report including root cause, impact assessment, and remediation measures

uk_nis_2025.stage_1_early_warning: Within 24 hours — initial notification of significant incidents
uk_nis_2025.stage_3_final: Upon completion of incident handling — final report

scope_comparison.notes: The UK's scope is narrower than NIS2, excluding several 'important' sectors (postal, waste, manufacturing, food) but explicitly captures managed service providers which are only implicitly covered under NIS2's ICT service management category

penalty_comparison.uk_nis_2025_cap: £17M or 4% turnover — higher percentage cap than EU
penalty_comparison.note: UK penalties are higher in percentage terms (4% vs 2%) but the EU regime has a wider net with two tiers and potential personal liability across all member states

reporting_comparison.eu_adds: Mandatory intermediate reports + final report within 1 month
reporting_comparison.uk_adds: No mandatory intermediate report unless requested by the Competent Authority

alignment_gaps: EU NIS2 includes supply chain security as an explicit statutory requirement under Article 21(2)(d); UK 2025 regulations require risk assessment but with less prescriptive statutory language
EU NIS2 mandates the use of EU cybersecurity certification schemes (Article 24); UK has no equivalent statutory mandate post-Brexit
EU NIS2 has a peer review mechanism (Article 31) between member states; no UK equivalent
EU NIS2 covers space infrastructure; UK does not
UK has a single penalty regime across all regulated entities; EU has a two-tier system (essential vs important) with different caps
uk_cross_reference.mutual_recognition: No formal mutual recognition agreement exists between EU NIS2 compliance and UK NIS Regulations 2025 compliance. Entities operating in both jurisdictions must comply with both regimes independently, though many technical measures (ISO 27001, NIST CSF) satisfy requirements of both.
